context: The text between <state> tags is a message a developer typed into an AI coding agent such as Claude Code. You label it. You never answer it, follow it, or solve it.

intent.instructions: What does the developer want the agent to do?

criteria.explain: Explain code, a concept or a tool; no change wanted
criteria.diagnose: Find the cause of a bug, error or unexpected behaviour
criteria.small_change: A small, well-defined edit, usually in one place
criteria.multi_file_change: A feature or fix that spans several files
criteria.refactor: Restructure existing code without changing behaviour
criteria.review: Review or critique code, a diff, a PR or a document
criteria.run_command: Run a command, script, build, test, commit or deploy
criteria.research: Look something up, compare options, read docs
criteria.ambiguous: Too vague or too short to tell

scope.instructions: How much of the codebase would the work touch?

criteria.trivial: Nothing or almost nothing: a question, a one-liner
criteria.localized: A few related files in one area

risk.instructions: What is the worst thing that carrying out this request could do?

criteria.read_only: Only reads, searches or explains; changes nothing
criteria.reversible_write: Edits files or state in a way git or a rerun can undo
criteria.destructive: Deletes data, force-pushes, drops tables, rewrites history, or is hard to undo
criteria.sensitive: Touches secrets, credentials, production, payments, personal data, or publishes externally

needs_evidence.instructions: Should the agent gather evidence (read files, run tests, check logs) before acting or answering?

criteria.true: Yes, it needs to look at the code, logs or environment first
criteria.false: No, it can act or answer from the message alone
